blocks.heading: Evaluate intervention against the problem
blocks.text: Evaluate an intervention by linking its objective, mechanism, beneficiaries, resource cost and possible unintended effects. A grant may make useful investment possible but also use public funds that could support another need. Support may be temporary while an underlying weakness persists. Compare plausible alternatives such as information, infrastructure or a targeted capability improvement. Ask whether the measure actually changes the constraint and whether outcomes can be reviewed. Do not judge success from the amount spent or the number of applications alone.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A scheme offers machines to Hela Foods, but its existing equipment has spare capacity and its main problem is unreliable transport to customers. Extra machines may add idle capacity without improving delivery. Targeted logistics support may be more relevant, subject to cost and evidence. Choose the intervention addressing access first rather than rewarding investment for its own sake.
